_comment: Declarative on purpose. This file describes WHICH scraped labels mean what;
it contains no code, and it is interpreted server-side rather than in the
browser. A pack must never be able to ship JavaScript into a content script:
installing a pack would then mean granting it the ability to run on every
The extension's job shrinks to: collect label/value pairs off the page and
POST them. Which labels matter, and what they mean, lives here — so a new
listing site is a JSON file, and a site redesign is a data edit rather than

fuel._comment: The technical panel writes 'Gasoline / EURO 6' and, when the fuel row is absent, hides the fuel inside 'Motor Tipi' / 'Engine Type' ('Gasoline / 4 cylinders'). Both are the first segment.

transmission._comment: 'Şanzıman / Çekiş' reads 'Otomatik / Önden Çekiş'; the English panel reads 'DSG / 7 Gear / Front Wheel Drive'. The gearbox is the first segment in both.

power_min_hp._comment: 'Maksimum Güç' reads '110 hp (81 kw) / 4,600 rpm'; the range bound is what makes reading the first number safe — 81 and 4600 are both outside it.

build_year._comment: Falls back to the title. The info-list markup here has been redesigned repeatedly and every redesign zeroed every field; the year is the one identity key a title reliably carries.

derive._comment: Age is arithmetic on the build year, not a scraped field.

_ignore_comment: These labels are not read at all, not merely left out of the coverage
report. Several of them are near-misses for a rule above — 'Yakıt
Tüketimi' contains 'yakıt', 'Motor Tipi' contains 'motor' — and the
extension no longer filters anything client-side, so this list is the
only thing that stops a consumption figure being read as a fuel type.
